page: Microsoft Azure L12aos_v4 is a storage-optimized virtual machine provisioned on Microsoft Hyper-V. It features the AMD EPYC 9V74 processor based on the x86_64 architecture, configured with 12 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 6 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. The CPU operates at an active frequency of 3.7 GHz and includes 32 KB L1 data cache, 1 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. It incorporates vector and cryptographic acceleration instructions, including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, AVX-512 BF16, AES, and SHA-NI. The instance is allocated 96.0 GB of memory (8.0 GB per vCPU) and bundles 8,639 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage. It operates without dedicated GPUs and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-core compute performance, highlighted by top-quartile results in stress-ng single-core (3,078.38) and Geekbench single-core tests (2,087.0). Multi-core throughput remains in the middle 50% tier, registering a PassMark CPU score of 20,559.19, a Geekbench multi-core score of 10,441.0, and a stress-ng multi-core output of 18,474.21. In memory assessments, small-block cached read throughput reaches 912.02 GB/sec, though uncached large-block reads fall into the bottom 25% at 38.93 GB/sec. Application tests show steady mid-range throughput, with 17.12 million operations per second in Redis SET workloads and 16.01 GB/sec in static web serving benchmarks.

The primary tradeoff of the L12aos_v4 lies in its memory subsystem latency over large sequential working sets versus its large NVMe storage capacity and high single-thread clock. The hardware profile is cost-efficient for applications requiring significant low-latency local disk space alongside substantial memory per core, avoiding external block storage overheads. It is well-fitted for high-I/O transactional databases, data warehousing, analytics platforms, distributed cache architectures, and log aggregation systems requiring direct access to fast NVMe SSD storage.
description: Microsoft Azure L12aos_v4 is a storage-optimized virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor at 3.7 GHz. Built on x86_64 architecture, it delivers 12 dedicated vCPUs (6 physical cores) and 96.0 GB of RAM, offering a high 8.0 GB memory-to-vCPU ratio. A key attribute is its bundled 8,639 GB local NVMe SSD storage array, operating without dedicated GPU hardware. CPU performance benchmarks show strong single-threaded execution, ranking in the top 25% on Geekbench and stress-ng single-core metrics, while multi-core workloads, PassMark CPU testing, and Redis operations place squarely in the middle 50%. Although uncached large-block memory read bandwidth ranks in the lower tier, the instance's high local I/O density and strong vector instruction set (AVX-512) provide efficient hardware economics for data-intensive applications. It is tailored for large transactional databases, distributed storage, data analytics, and search indexing nodes.
